run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The only incident evidence available is the four documents in the Elasticsearch index app-267-prod-logs (cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment prod, region eu-west-1 — the cluster named in the question). They describe a consistent chain: at 2026-11-21T04:34:12Z checkout-service logs ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)' and payment-service logs ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms' at the same second; at 05:34:12Z checkout-service logs ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)'; at 06:04:12Z payment-service logs WARN 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620'. On that evidence the deepest identified cause is the external payment provider adyen-eu, which is not a Kubernetes object in this cluster (no Service, Deployment or ConfigMap named adyen-eu or mentioning 'adyen' was returned), so it could not be inspected directly. The alternative fault-injection explanation was checked and rejected: the flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo defines paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant 'off'. Counter-evidence on identity/scope: the log-service names checkout-service and payment-service match no Deployment or OTel service name in the cluster, and the in-cluster otel-demo checkout/payment pods show successful PlaceOrder/charge flows sampled at 04:31-04:39Z and again at 05:34:34Z and 05:56:08Z, so their own logs do not corroborate the index errors. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every query in this run, so POST /api/checkout error rate, span errors and latency could not be measured; that is why the conclusion is partial rather than supported end-to-end.

claims.text: Index app-267-prod-logs contains 4 documents (docs.count=4) and a match_all search over the authorized window returned exactly 4 documents, all tagged cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1, with timestamps from 2026-11-21T04:34:12Z to 2026-11-21T06:04:12Z.
At 2026-11-21T04:34:12Z service checkout-service logged level=ERROR: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)'.

At the same second 2026-11-21T04:34:12Z service payment-service logged level=ERROR: 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms', i.e. payment-service's own error names adyen-eu /v68/payments as the upstream that timed out.
At 2026-11-21T05:34:12Z service checkout-service logged level=ERROR: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)', one hour after the first checkout 500.
At 2026-11-21T06:04:12Z service payment-service logged level=WARN: 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620', the latest document in the index.

No Kubernetes object named adyen-eu exists in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1: the 30 Services returned (all namespaces) contain no adyen service, the 26 Deployments returned contain no adyen workload, and a cluster-wide ConfigMap query (23 items processed) matched no ConfigMap whose name contains adyen/payment/checkout or whose data contains 'adyen'.

The otel-demo checkout container is configured with PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and the otel-demo payment container carries only PAYMENT_PORT, FLAGD_HOST and FLAGD_PORT — no container env in the otel-demo Deployments references adyen or any external payment provider.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) defines fault-injection flags with names/descriptions that refer to payment: 'paymentFailure' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and 'paymentUnreachable' ('Payment service is unavailable'); both are declared with defaultVariant 'off' in the copy read at query time.

Every otel-demo container's last termination is identical: exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, with containers restarted between 04:23:47Z and 04:24:34Z (kube-state-metrics exited 1 at 04:24:17Z, nginx proxy exited 1 at 04:24:10Z), i.e. a cluster-wide container restart 10 minutes before the first ES error and with no checkout-specific reason.

The otel-demo payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (container 'payment') logged 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' for every charge sampled between 2026-11-21T04:31:19Z and 04:39:55Z, with no error line in that sample — including 04:35:04Z, 04:38:43Z and 04:39:55Z, i.e. after the 04:34:12Z timeout reported in app-267-prod-logs.

The otel-demo checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged successful '[PlaceOrder]' -> 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' -> 'order confirmation email sent' sequences between 04:31:19Z and 04:39:55Z, and its last-hour log read returned 'order confirmation email sent' at 05:34:34Z and 'payment went through' at 05:56:08Z, i.e. successful orders across the 05:34:12Z 'Circuit-breaker open' timestamp in the index.

Namespace app-282 contains a transient 'checkout' Deployment (python:3.9-slim plus a grafana/promtail:2.9.0 sidecar) and a 'loki' Deployment; events show ReplicaSets checkout-698c8f5df and loki-66445c6d6f scaled 0->1 at 06:33:18-06:33:19Z and pod checkout-698c8f5df-bcps9 created and its containers started at 06:33:19-06:33:20Z — after all four incident log documents — and these objects are not related by any evidence to the checkout errors.

Primary causal chain: degradation of the external payment provider adyen-eu (30s response timeouts on /v68/payments, degraded mode acknowledged, retry queue depth 620) caused payment-service upstream timeouts, which surfaced at the edge as 500s on POST /api/checkout from checkout-service and then tripped checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service at a 36% failure rate.

Rejected: flagd fault-injection flags as the cause of the payment failures. The candidate settings are paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') in ConfigMap flagd-config; both are declared defaultVariant 'off' in the copy read at 06:34Z, they are not switched on in the evidence, and neither reproduces the observed text 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms'.

Rejected as the cause: the cluster-wide container termination at 04:23:42Z. It hit every otel-demo container identically (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown') including flagd, prometheus, jaeger and kube-state-metrics, is 10 minutes earlier than the first checkout/payment error, and the error text names a specific external upstream rather than a local restart; the restart is a change in the window but is not shown to have caused the checkout failures.

Rejected: Kubernetes-level unavailability of the in-cluster payment endpoint as the mechanism (e.g. missing service/pods). Service payment exists in otel-demo (ClusterIP, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, port 8080), pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Running and Ready with no restart since 04:23:48Z, and its application logs show completed transactions, so the timeout is recorded against an external upstream, not a dead in-cluster endpoint.

Counter-evidence to treating the otel-demo checkout/payment workloads as the affected entities: the log documents' service names are 'checkout-service' and 'payment-service', while the cluster's Deployments are named checkout and payment (otel-demo, OTel service.name=checkout/payment, PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080) and no Deployment or Service named checkout-service/payment-service was returned; the sampled application logs of those pods show successful orders/charges at the same times the index reports failures (04:31-04:39Z, 05:34:34Z, 05:56:08Z).

Treat this as an external provider incident: confirm adyen-eu's status page/incident record for the 04:34-06:04Z period, check payment-service's retry queue depth trend (620 at 06:04Z) and its 30s timeout/circuit-breaker thresholds, and decide on provider failover or traffic shedding; these are advisory only and were not executed.

Establish the mapping between the documents in app-267-prod-logs and cluster workloads (which shipper/agent writes service=checkout-service and service=payment-service), because no Deployment, Service or ConfigMap in acme-prod-eu-west-1 carries those names; until then, impact statements about specific pods cannot be verified.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every query in this run — metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query (twice), get_metric_names and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE — so the POST /api/checkout 500/error rate, the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state, and any latency comparison against a baseline could not be measured; no latency trend is asserted.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so span-level payment->adyen-eu calls and the checkout PlaceOrder error spans named in the log index could not be inspected, and the affected/unaffected split cannot be confirmed from traces.

adyen-eu is outside Kubernetes: no Service, Deployment, ConfigMap, metric, trace or log for it was available, so its own degradation is known only from the checkout-service and payment-service statements in app-267-prod-logs and could not be verified directly.

No workload, Service or ConfigMap in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 is named checkout-service or payment-service; which deployment/log shipper emitted those documents is unknown, and the in-cluster otel-demo checkout/payment pods' own logs do not show matching errors in the sampled periods.

What triggered the simultaneous container termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', across all otel-demo pods plus the control-plane pods restarting at 04:23:43Z) is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The exact time window of the incident is only bounded by the four log documents (04:34:12Z to 06:04:12Z); whether failures continued after 06:04:12Z is unknown because the index has no later documents.

The app-282 namespace objects (checkout-698c8f5df-bcps9, loki-66445c6d6f-7nwbp) seen being created at 06:33:18-06:33:21Z were no longer returned by a deployments/pods read at 06:35Z (those reads returned no data / POD_NOT_FOUND), so their purpose and lifecycle are unknown.
Frontend-side evidence could not be checked: the frontend pod's log read returned no data (no lines read), so 500s on POST /api/checkout at the frontend layer were not observed either way.
The NetworkPolicy query returned no data, so it is unknown whether any network policy exists that could affect payment/checkout traffic; resource quota state was not examined.
Secrets (e.g. payment provider credentials or endpoints) cannot be read, so provider configuration values could not be verified.
next_steps: Check adyen-eu's status page/incident history for 2026-11-21 04:30-06:30Z to confirm the provider-side degradation independently.

Have the owner of the app-267-prod-logs pipeline identify the workloads behind service=checkout-service and service=payment-service, and confirm whether they are the otel-demo checkout/payment deployments or a separate app-267 environment.

Re-run the Prometheus queries (checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, rpc_client_duration for payment, traces_span_metrics_calls_total) and Jaeger trace lookups once those sources are reachable, to quantify the 500 rate and fix the start/end time of the incident.
Ask the platform team what caused the cluster-wide container restart at 04:23:42Z and whether it was planned maintenance.

{"alertmanager.yml":"global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        credentials_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        type: Bearer
    max_alerts: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
"}

{"relay":"connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      authenticator: basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
